topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russia and Ukraine agreed a large prisoner-of-war exchange as two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended, but envoys announced no major breakthrough on ending the war. Zelensky said he welcomed a change in the U.S. approach, and Kushner and Witkoff are reportedly pushing a NATO-like security guarantee for Ukraine. Strikes on energy infrastructure continued, with a Ukrainian drone attack reportedly starting a fire at the Ust-Luga Baltic oil hub, and Russia banned two French lawmakers and two journalists in a tit-for-tat move.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Iran reportedly vowed not to let any enriched nuclear material leave the country (Reuters, dated Nov 11), while single-source reporting describes a U.S. blockade on Iran and a reported split between Rubio (backing the blockade) and Vance (favouring a deal). An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, killing six and wounding more than 20, and further strikes continue despite the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire. Saudi Arabia reported October crude output of 10.563 million bpd, near pre-war levels. See also the Bessent item under embassy/diplomat threats.
topics.T15: Coverage is scattered and mostly minor. A landslide in Zeballos, British Columbia, has produced evacuation orders expected to last through Friday amid forecast heavy rain, and a 4.5-magnitude earthquake near Eilat briefly halted aviation at Ramon Airport. Other items are a UN early-warning report released at COP31 and Indonesia earthquake aid, with no clear access-denial event.
topics.T01: The stories are too varied to form a single narrative. Reported items include a Reuters-sourced account of a Vance meeting with an oil trader before the Venezuela operation, fears of renewed fighting in Tigray, a G7 foreign ministers' statement from Paris, and the detention of Sudanese figure Ahmed Haroun amid the ongoing Sudan war. The cyber-linked hoax bomb story is covered under cyber.
topics.T02: Stories are sparse and generic: a Nigerian mobile ID registration drive for 3.7 million displaced persons, a Vinícius Júnior invitation to a Sudanese boy who lost both legs, a pneumococcal vaccination modelling study, a U.S. bill on VA assessments of toxic hazards in combat zones, and a Qatari meeting with the UN children and armed conflict envoy. No significant new crisis is evident.
topics.T03: Nine nations pledged to align with the EU's extended chemical weapons sanctions; no further detail was provided.
topics.T04: Five outlets report that Kenya refused to serve as an Ebola quarantine hub for travelers, though the provided text gives no further detail. Oregon reported its first highly pathogenic avian influenza detection at a dairy, in Morrow County, and Hillsborough County, Florida, reported 22 new local dengue cases for a total of 407. The remaining items are research papers and a prison scabies controversy.
topics.T05: US Defense Secretary Hegseth publicly defied an impeachment effort as the House prepared to vote on eight articles against him. President Trump renewed the national emergency declaration on Nicaragua, and Bangladesh MP Nusrat Tabassum alleged petrol bombs were thrown at her home amid tension over Sheikh Hasina's planned return. Nigerian opposition (ADC) protesters also demanded release of a court judgment.
topics.T06: Tens of thousands marched across Spain in a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power, with clashes reported, weeks before an early general election. A separate single-source item cites a poll in which eight in ten French voters blame the Macron government for recent riots.
topics.T07: France reportedly fears that German long-range missiles could trigger nuclear escalation with Russia, as Europe builds up its conventional deterrent. The E-4B 'Nightwatch' airborne command post reportedly flew from Offutt Air Force Base on Nov. 5, per flight-tracking data cited by the Daily Mail, which offers no confirmed explanation. See also Iran's uranium statement under the Middle East flagship.
topics.T08: A militant ambush in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killed at least 10 police personnel including a DSP, with a gunbattle reportedly still under way. In Indian-administered Kashmir, three CRPF personnel were wounded in a checkpost shooting in Kulgam. Other items include a UN report alleging the UAE sent Colombian mercenaries to support Sudan's RSF and a look at foreign forces and militias fighting gangs in Haiti.
topics.T10: Sen. Kevin Cramer called on Nvidia's CEO to resign over alleged extortion risks tied to a suspected Chinese spy, and records reportedly show a blacklisted PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite U.S export controls. A U.S. general warned Madagascar over growing military ties with Russia, and Poland's state armaments group is central to its rearmament drive.
topics.T11: India began the 15th Naseem Al Bahr naval exercise with Oman, with INS Surat arriving in Muscat, and the India-Myanmar exercise IMNEX-26 began in Visakhapatnam, running to November 14. A single-source analysis describes a PLA 'silent' exercise practicing dispersal of naval forces and breakout into the Western Pacific.
topics.T12: About 6,300 Italian schools received hoax bomb warnings and were evacuated, with similar alerts reported in the UK and Ireland, part of a series of threats and cyberattacks across Europe hitting supermarkets, blood banks, air traffic and broadcasters. Romania's intelligence agency said it identified a Russian-linked cyberattack. CISA flagged active exploitation of a Cisco BroadWorks flaw, and a ransomware gang claimed a Vanderbilt University breach, which is unverified.
topics.T13: Stories are generic and mixed, covering UK asylum hotel contracts, U.S. immigration enforcement and politics, and Spain's VOX calling for remigration. An INTERPOL operation against Mediterranean and West African migrant-smuggling networks led to 262 arrests.
topics.T14: Five outlets carry an analysis asking whether Iran is expanding retaliation to Western soil, tied to the relocation of Treasury Secretary Bessent from the U.S. to the EU, with an expert saying the expansion may be deliberate. Separately, a zero-source report says the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert over Houthi attack threats and ordered non-emergency staff and families to leave. That report is unconfirmed by the provided material.
topics.T16: Brazil's electoral court fined Meta 7.5 million but found no deliberate election bias. Other items include post-midterm U.S. political fallout, a Shin Bet probe into foreign election interference, India's Election Commission rejecting claims of vote-count discrepancies, and Cabo Verde's upcoming presidential election.

bluf: Roughly 6,300 Italian schools were evacuated after receiving hoax bomb warnings, with similar alerts reported in the UK and Ireland, the latest in a series of threats and cyberattacks hitting European infrastructure. Russia and Ukraine agreed a large prisoner-of-war exchange as U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi concluded, but no breakthrough on ending the war was announced. Five outlets are carrying an analysis, tied to Treasury Secretary Bessent's relocation from the U.S. to the EU, that asks whether Iran is deliberately extending its retaliation campaign beyond the Middle East. The provided text offers few details and no confirmation. Tens of thousands marched in a nationwide general strike in Spain over housing costs and purchasing power, with clashes reported, weeks before an early general election. France reportedly fears that German long-range missiles could trigger nuclear escalation with Russia, as Europe builds a stronger conventional deterrent. Separately, a zero-source, unverified report says the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh ordered non-emergency staff and families to leave over Houthi threats. In Pakistan, a militant ambush in Kohat killed at least 10 police, including a DSP.
